title: Choose ChatLaw’s visual world
question: The roll assigned DigiLocker Civic Portal for Chat (citizen Operate). Keep it, take an alternate, re-roll, or play the category straight.

options.label: DigiLocker Civic Portal
options.lineage: DigiLocker, passport e-services, and bilingual Indian gov portals
options.thesis: ChatLaw as the civic service desk citizens already trust: issued answers, stamped citations, bilingual chrome.
options.viewport: Desktop Chat: navy service rail left, white content well with interview thread, answer card as an issued document with section citations as stamped fields, language chip in the header.
options.risk: Feels bureaucratic or cold if citizen warmth is lost to portal seriousness.

raised.raise: Statute text and section numbers are the visual matter — citations form the answer body, not bolted-on badges.
Every zone carries a literal functional name; wayfinding is reading.
Conversation history stays visible as marks on the surface, not a disposable thread.
Strict modular grid — no off-grid decorative chrome.
Interview and loading steps read as fixed-place status counters.

options.label: India Code Section Browser
options.lineage: India Code / Legislative Department statute browsers
options.thesis: The assistant that looks like reading the Code itself: hierarchical sections beside the interview.
options.viewport: Chat with a live Code rail of retrieved sections flanking the plain-language interview.
options.risk: Also the direction most legal-assistant runs land on — familiar and effective.

options.label: High-Density Module Mosaic
options.thesis: Legal chat as a packed mosaic of ruled modules: questions, citations, and actions each own a box.
options.viewport: Chat as a dense CSS mosaic: history, answer, citations, and composer as abutting ruled modules with red state tabs.
options.case: Holds Operate clarity through density; loses audience identification to DigiLocker for Indian citizens.
options.risk: Crowds a stressed citizen if modules shout at equal scale.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: Letters condense into legal answers like weather systems.
options.viewport: Chat where typed words gather into citation clouds.
options.case: Loses audience identification and Operate clarity for a stressed legal task.
options.kept: Statute text treated as visual matter.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.thesis: Every zone named in straight quotes with hazard structure.
options.viewport: Quoted zone labels over a stockroom-white chat.
options.case: Loses both axes for citizen legal trust.
options.kept: Literal zone naming; wayfinding is reading.

options.label: Flash Scrawl Sleeve
options.thesis: Defaced flash photo as the chat surface.
options.viewport: A defaced surface where marks accumulate as history.
options.case: Wrong cultural home for Indian legal assistance.
options.kept: History as visible marks on the surface.

options.label: Arcade Pixel Glow
options.thesis: Legal chat as a luminous pixel playfield.
options.case: Loses both axes for legal Operate.

options.label: Nixie Laboratory Counter
options.thesis: Quantities glow as plasma digits in glass.
options.viewport: Metrics as tube banks beside the thread.
options.risk: Lab toy, not a legal desk.

canonCard.label: Category-standard legal assistant
canonCard.thesis: Clean SaaS legal-chat chrome executed at full craft — the familiar competitor path.
canonCard.viewport: Left nav, centered chat column, citation chips — what visitors expect from AI legal tools.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from neighboring products by design.
